howTo.setup: Pick one new experience from the checklist. Have tasty treats ready and choose a distance at which she stays relaxed: loose body, wagging tail, curious.
steps: Let her watch the new thing from that distance; every time she looks at it calmly, say “good” and give a treat.
Let her choose to get closer; never carry or pull her toward it.
If she sniffs or explores on her own, praise her quietly and keep the treats coming.
Stop after a few minutes, while she is still relaxed, and go somewhere calm.
howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed and curious 4 times out of 5: get a little closer, or make it a little louder or longer, one change at a time.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she freezes, tucks her tail, hides or will not take treats, she is too close: move away calmly until she relaxes, and next time start farther away.
howTo.mistakes: Forcing her to face what scares her, too many new things in one day, and missing the signs of fear.

howTo.setup: A calm moment, ideally after a nap or a walk. Small treats at hand and a soft surface where she can sit or lie down.
steps: Touch a paw for one second, say “good” and give a treat. Do the same with an ear.
Little by little, hold the paw a bit longer, gently spread the toes and look inside the ear.
Reward every touch, even the short ones, and stop before she tries to pull away.
Practice what the vet will do: lift her lips to see her teeth, touch her belly and her tail.
howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed 4 times out of 5: hold a little longer, or bring a towel or a brush she can see and sniff first.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she pulls away or mouths your hand, you went too fast: go back to a shorter touch she accepts and reward more often.
howTo.mistakes: Holding her down while she struggles, handling her only when something has to be done, and long sessions.

howTo.setup: A soft brush and a few treats. A quiet moment in the evening, before bed.
steps: Let her sniff the brush and give her a treat.
Make one short stroke along her back, say “good” and give a treat.
Add strokes one at a time along her back and sides, in the direction of the coat.
Stop after a minute or two, while she is calm, and finish with a gentle game.
howTo.levelUp: She stays calm 4 times out of 5: brush a little longer and add her chest, legs and tail.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she bites the brush or wriggles, give her a chew toy to hold, go back to one stroke and reward more often.
howTo.mistakes: Brushing against the coat, pulling on knots, and brushing for a long time when she is excited.

howTo.setup: First weeks: a pen in the barn, out of draughts, with a raised bed, dry bedding, her litter blanket and a chew toy. The outdoor kennel comes later, step by step.
steps: During the day, toss treats into the pen and let her go in and out freely; say “good” when she goes in.
Give her a meal or a chew toy inside, so the pen means good things.
At bedtime, follow the same calm routine every night: potty, a short quiet moment, then to the pen with her blanket.
The first 2 or 3 nights, stay nearby until she settles; until 12 weeks, take her out once in the middle of the night.
Later, move to the kennel little by little: daytime naps first, then nights, when she is older and the weather is mild.
howTo.levelUp: She settles 4 nights out of 5: keep the routine short and at the same time every night.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she cries, check calmly that she does not need to go potty and that she is warm and dry, then leave again without playing; on cold nights follow the cold alert.
howTo.mistakes: Using the pen or the kennel as a punishment, long goodbyes, changing the routine every night, and moving her outside alone in the coldest weeks.

howTo.setup: The cats loose, with high places and exits she cannot reach; their food and litter out of her reach. Dela in her pen or on a leash, with treats at hand.
steps: Let them see and smell each other through the pen; every time she looks at a cat calmly, say “good” and give a treat.
If she barks, whines or lunges, she is too excited: take her a little farther away and reward her when she calms down.
Once she watches them calmly, take her out on a leash for short meetings; the cat decides whether to come closer.
Practice “leave it” with a cat in sight and reward her for looking back at you.
Stop after a few minutes, before she gets excited; do not leave them loose together unsupervised yet.
howTo.levelUp: She stays calm 4 times out of 5: get a little closer, then use a long line, then short supervised moments loose in the barn.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she chases a cat, calmly go back to the leash and more distance; if a cat hisses or hides, give it space and make the next meeting shorter.
howTo.mistakes: Letting her chase “to play”, holding a cat close to her face, scolding her, and leaving them alone together too soon.

howTo.setup: A calm moment after a walk and a potty break, when she is sleepy. Her pen with a chew toy or a food toy.
steps: Give her the chew toy in the pen and walk out of sight for a few seconds, then come back calmly.
Come back while she is still calm, before she cries, and greet her quietly, without a party.
Add a little time each day: 10 seconds, 30 seconds, a minute, a few minutes.
Leave and come back calmly, with no long goodbyes, so comings and goings are boring.
howTo.levelUp: She stays calm 4 times out of 5: add a little more time, then leave the barn for a moment and come back.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she cries as soon as you leave, it was too long too soon: go back to a few seconds and build up again; check first that she does not need to go potty.
howTo.mistakes: Leaving her alone for hours from the first day, making a fuss when you leave or come back, and always coming back while she is crying.
